title: SharePoint: mark sites as authoritative so Copilot prioritises their content
summary: Hold: Restricted Content Discovery does not keep a site's content out of every Copilot experience, as the briefing suggests. The advice also assumes a separate 100-site allowance per geo without a stating passage, and the rationales promise administrator-only activation despite an unknown default. The listed admin paths and PowerShell command are documented.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: Marking a site promotes whatever it holds, including stale or overshared files, and labels all that content From your organization.
claims.quote: Searched: '"authoritative sites" "all content" "no action"'; '"authoritative sites" "content" "permissions" "Restricted Content Discovery"'. Opened authoritative-sites and release-notes. Neither guarantees promotion and labelling of every file.
claims.fix: Replace the factual premise in both sections with: 'Copilot Search recognises content from marked sites as trusted. This makes reviewing candidate sites for stale or overshared content important.' Do not say that every file is promoted or labelled.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery can keep a site out of Copilot.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.
claims.fix: Replace 'to keep a site out of Copilot instead' with 'to limit a site's discoverability in organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios instead'. Add: 'Restricted Content Discovery does not prevent Copilot from summarising an open document.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The feature takes no action on content.
claims.quote: Searched: '"authoritative sites" "all content" "no action"'. Opened authoritative-sites and the feature's release-note entry. They describe administrator designation and search effects, not an exhaustive guarantee of no content actions.
claims.fix: Replace 'No change: the feature is a designation administrators set on sites; it takes no action on content' with 'The documented operation is an administrator setting an authoritative designation on a site.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A multi-geo tenant can shortlist up to 100 authoritative sites per geo.
claims.quote: Searched: '"authoritative sites" "100" "geo"'. Opened authoritative-sites and release-notes. Learn separately states a 100-site limit and per-geo data management; it does not state that each geo receives its own 100-site allowance.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'Shortlist no more than 100 sites, starting with policy, HR and news sites. In multi-geo tenants, manage authoritative site data per geo.' Do not attach 'per geo' to the numerical allowance.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The default is unknown, but the rationales assert that authoritative designation and user-visible changes happen only after administrator marking.
claims.quote: defaultState: "unknown"; "Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival"; "A site becomes authoritative only when an administrator marks it"; "users notice only once sites are marked"
claims.fix: Keep defaultState as unknown: searches for 'SharePoint authoritative sites default enabled tenant Set-SPOTenant IsAuthoritative default' and '"authoritative sites" "default" "automatically" "before"' found no stated arrival default. Replace the risk rationale with 'Low. The default is not stated, so this assessment assumes today's behaviour continues. Microsoft describes marked sites as trusted sources in Copilot Search.' Replace the impact rationale with 'Low. The documented change is an administrator designation, with ranking and visual signals in Copilot Search. Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival.'
